sanskrit: paśya śāṃtanavaṃ kṛṣṇa śayānaṃ sūryavarcasam yugānta iva kālena pātitaṃ sūryam ambarāt
english: Behold, O Kṛṣṇa, the son of Śaṃtanu lying there, radiant as the sun, cast down as the sun is cast from the sky by Time at the ending of an age.

sanskrit: eṣa taptvā raṇe śatrūñ śastratāpena vīryavān narasūryo 'stam abhyeti sūryo 'stam iva keśava
english: This valiant one, having scorched his foes in battle with the heat of his weapons, this sun among men now goes to his setting, O Keśava, as the sun goes to its setting.

sanskrit: śaratalpagataṃ vīraṃ dharme devāpinā samam śayānaṃ vīraśayane paśya śūraniṣevite
english: Behold the hero who has gone to his bed of arrows, the equal of Devāpi in righteousness, lying upon the warrior's couch that is the haunt of brave men.

sanskrit: karṇinālīkanārācair āstīrya śayanottamam āviśya śete bhagavān skandaḥ śaravaṇaṃ yathā
english: Having strewn his lordly couch with barbed shafts, nālīka darts, and iron arrows, he lies upon it, like the divine Skanda couched amid the reed-thicket of his birth.

sanskrit: atūlapūrṇaṃ gāṅgeyas tribhir bāṇaiḥ samanvitam upadhāyopadhānāgryaṃ dattaṃ gāṇḍīvadhanvanā
english: The son of Gaṅgā rests his head upon no pillow stuffed with down, but upon a fine bolster of three arrows given to him by the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva bow.

sanskrit: pālayānaḥ pituḥ śāstram ūrdhvaretā mahāyaśāḥ eṣa śāṃtanavaḥ śete mādhavāpratimo yudhi
english: Keeping his father's command, of seed drawn upward and of mighty fame, this son of Śaṃtanu lies here, O Mādhava, who had no equal in war.

sanskrit: dharmātmā tāta dharmajñaḥ pāraṃparyeṇa nirṇaye amartya iva martyaḥ sann eṣa prāṇān adhārayat
english: Righteous of soul, my dear one, knowing the law and its decision by the lineage of tradition, though mortal he held to his life-breaths as though he were a deathless one.

sanskrit: nāsti yuddhe kṛtī kaś cin na vidvān na parākramī yatra śāṃtanavo bhīṣmaḥ śete 'dya nihataḥ paraiḥ
english: There is none now skilled in war, none learned, none of prowess, since Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu lies slain this day by his foes.

sanskrit: svayam etena śūreṇa pṛcchyamānena pāṇḍavaiḥ dharmajñenāhave mṛtyur ākhyātaḥ satyavādinā
english: By this hero himself, the knower of the law, the speaker of truth, when the Pāṇḍavas questioned him, the manner of his own death in battle was told.

sanskrit: pranaṣṭaḥ kuruvaṃśaś ca punar yena samuddhṛtaḥ sa gataḥ kurubhiḥ sārdhaṃ mahābuddhiḥ parābhavam
english: He by whom the perished line of Kuru was once again raised up, that man of vast wisdom has gone, together with the Kurus, to ruin.

sanskrit: dharmeṣu kuravaḥ kaṃ nu pariprakṣyanti mādhava gate devavrate svargaṃ devakalpe nararṣabhe
english: Whom now, O Mādhava, shall the Kurus question concerning matters of the law, when Devavrata, that bull among men, godlike in nature, has gone to heaven?

sanskrit: arjunasya vinetāram ācāryaṃ sātyakes tathā taṃ paśya patitaṃ droṇaṃ kurūṇāṃ gurusattamam
english: Behold him fallen, Droṇa, the teacher who trained Arjuna and Sātyaki alike, the most excellent of the Kurus' preceptors.

sanskrit: astraṃ caturvidhaṃ veda yathaiva tridaśeśvaraḥ bhārgavo vā mahāvīryas tathā droṇo 'pi mādhava
english: The fourfold science of weapons he knew, even as the lord of the thirty gods knows it, or as the mighty descendant of Bhṛgu knew it; such was Droṇa too, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: yasya prasādād bībhatsuḥ pāṇḍavaḥ karma duṣkaram cakāra sa hataḥ śete nainam astrāṇy apālayan
english: He by whose grace Bībhatsu the Pāṇḍava wrought his deeds hard to accomplish lies slain; his own weapons did not protect him.

sanskrit: yaṃ purodhāya kurava āhvayanti sma pāṇḍavān so 'yaṃ śastrabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭho droṇaḥ śastraiḥ pṛthak kṛtaḥ
english: He whom the Kurus set at their head when they challenged the Pāṇḍavas, that same Droṇa, foremost of weapon-bearers, has been cut apart by weapons.

sanskrit: yasya nirdahataḥ senāṃ gatir agner ivābhavat sa bhūmau nihataḥ śete śāntārcir iva pāvakaḥ
english: He whose course, as he burned the army, was like the course of fire, lies slain upon the earth like a flame whose blaze has died away.

sanskrit: dhanur muṣṭir aśīrṇaś ca hastāvāpaś ca mādhava droṇasya nihatasyāpi dṛśyate jīvato yathā
english: His bow, his grip undecayed, and the leather guard upon his hand, O Mādhava, are seen upon Droṇa even slain, as if he yet lived.

sanskrit: vedā yasmāc ca catvāraḥ sarvāstrāṇi ca keśava anapetāni vai śūrād yathaivādau prajāpateḥ
english: From this hero the four Vedas and all the weapons have not departed, O Keśava, even as in the beginning they did not depart from Prajāpati.

sanskrit: vandanārhāv imau tasya bandibhir vanditau śubhau gomāyavo vikarṣanti pādau śiṣyaśatārcitau
english: These his two fair feet, worthy of homage, praised by bards, honored by hundreds of his pupils, the jackals now drag about.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ drupadaputreṇa nihataṃ madhusūdana kṛpī kṛpaṇam anvāste duḥkhopahatacetanā
english: Beside Droṇa, slain by the son of Drupada, O slayer of Madhu, Kṛpī sits in piteous grief, her senses overborne by sorrow.

sanskrit: tāṃ paśya rudatīm ārtāṃ muktakeśīm adhomukhīm hataṃ patim upāsantīṃ droṇaṃ śastrabhṛtāṃ varam
english: Behold her, weeping and anguished, her hair unbound, her face cast down, attending upon her slain husband Droṇa, best of those who bear arms.

sanskrit: bāṇair bhinnatanutrāṇaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnena keśava upāste vai mṛdhe droṇaṃ jaṭilā brahmacāriṇī
english: Beside Droṇa, his armor pierced through by the arrows of Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O Keśava, sits she upon the field, her hair matted, faithful and chaste.

sanskrit: pretakṛtye ca yatate kṛpī kṛpaṇam āturā hatasya samare bhartuḥ sukumārī yaśasvinī
english: And Kṛpī, delicate and renowned, stricken and forlorn, strives to perform the funeral rites of her lord slain in battle.

sanskrit: agnīn āhṛtya vidhivac citāṃ prajvālya sarvaśaḥ droṇam ādhāya gāyanti trīṇi sāmāni sāmagāḥ
english: Bringing the sacred fires as the rite ordains and kindling the pyre on every side, the chanters of the Sāman lay Droṇa upon it and sing the three Sāman melodies.

sanskrit: kiranti ca citām ete jaṭilā brahmacāriṇaḥ dhanurbhiḥ śaktibhiś caiva rathanīḍaiś ca mādhava
english: And these matted-haired celibate students heap the pyre with bows, with spears, and with the framework-seats of chariots, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: śastraiś ca vividhair anyair dhakṣyante bhūritejasam ta ete droṇam ādhāya śaṃsanti ca rudanti ca
english: And with diverse other weapons they will burn that man of abundant splendor; having laid Droṇa down, they both chant his praises and weep.

sanskrit: sāmabhis tribhir antaḥsthair anuśaṃsanti cāpare agnāv agnim ivādhāya droṇaṃ hutvā hutāśane
english: And others sing his praises with the three Sāman chants set within, as though laying fire upon fire, offering Droṇa as oblation into the eater of offerings.

sanskrit: gacchanty abhimukhā gaṅgāṃ droṇaśiṣyā dvijātayaḥ apasavyāṃ citiṃ kṛtvā puraskṛtya kṛpīṃ tadā
english: Then the twice-born pupils of Droṇa go toward the Gaṅgā, keeping the pyre on their right hand and setting Kṛpī before them.

sanskrit: gāndhāry uvāca somadattasutaṃ paśya yuyudhānena pātitam vitudyamānaṃ vihagair bahubhir mādhavāntike
english: Gāndhārī said: Behold the son of Somadatta, struck down by Yuyudhāna, his body torn by many birds there beside Mādhava.

sanskrit: putraśokābhisaṃtaptaḥ somadatto janārdana yuyudhānaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ garhayann iva dṛśyate
english: Consumed by grief for his son, Somadatta, O Janārdana, is seen as though reproaching the great archer Yuyudhāna.

sanskrit: asau tu bhūriśravaso mātā śokapariplutā āśvāsayati bhartāraṃ somadattam aninditā
english: And there the blameless mother of Bhūriśravas, drowned in sorrow, seeks to console her husband Somadatta.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā nedaṃ mahārāja dāruṇaṃ bharatakṣayam kurusaṃkrandanaṃ ghoraṃ yugāntam anupaśyasi
english: "By fortune, great king, you do not look upon this terrible destruction of the Bharatas, this dreadful wailing of the Kurus, this ending of an age."

sanskrit: diṣṭyā yūpadhvajaṃ vīraṃ putraṃ bhūrisahasradam anekakratuyajvānaṃ nihataṃ nādya paśyasi
english: "By fortune you do not this day behold slain your heroic son, whose banner bore the sacrificial post, giver of many thousands, performer of many sacrifices."

sanskrit: diṣṭyā snuṣāṇām ākrande ghoraṃ vilapitaṃ bahu na śṛṇoṣi mahārāja sārasīnām ivārṇave
english: "By fortune, great king, you do not hear amid the outcry of your daughters-in-law their many dreadful laments, like the cries of cranes upon the ocean."

sanskrit: ekavastrānusaṃvītāḥ prakīrṇāsitamūrdhajāḥ snuṣās te paridhāvanti hatāpatyā hateśvarāḥ
english: Wrapped in a single garment, their dark hair flying loose, your daughters-in-law run about, their children slain and their lords slain.

sanskrit: śvāpadair bhakṣyamāṇaṃ tvam aho diṣṭyā na paśyasi chinnabāhuṃ naravyāghram arjunena nipātitam
english: Ah, by fortune you do not see him devoured by beasts of prey, that tiger among men, his arm severed, struck down by Arjuna.

sanskrit: śalaṃ vinihataṃ saṃkhye bhūriśravasam eva ca snuṣāś ca vidhavāḥ sarvā diṣṭyā nādyeha paśyasi
english: Śala slain in battle, and Bhūriśravas too, and all your daughters-in-law made widows: by fortune you do not behold them here this day.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tat kāñcanaṃ chatraṃ yūpaketor mahātmanaḥ vinikīrṇaṃ rathopasthe saumadatter na paśyasi
english: By fortune you do not see that golden parasol of the high-souled one whose banner bore the sacrificial post, flung down upon the chariot-seat of Somadatta's son.

sanskrit: amūs tu bhūriśravaso bhāryāḥ sātyakinā hatam parivāryānuśocanti bhartāram asitekṣaṇāḥ
english: And there the dark-eyed wives of Bhūriśravas, gathered round their husband slain by Sātyaki, grieve over him.

sanskrit: etā vilapya bahulaṃ bhartṛśokena karśitāḥ patanty abhimukhā bhūmau kṛpaṇaṃ bata keśava
english: Wailing long and wasted with grief for their husband, they fall forward upon the earth, piteously, alas, O Keśava.

sanskrit: bībhatsur atibībhatsaṃ karmedam akarot katham pramattasya yad acchaitsīd bāhuṃ śūrasya yajvanaḥ
english: How did Bībhatsu do this most loathsome deed, that he should sever the arm of an unguarded hero, a man of sacrifice?

sanskrit: tataḥ pāpataraṃ karma kṛtavān api sātyakiḥ yasmāt prāyopaviṣṭasya prāhārṣīt saṃśitātmanaḥ
english: And Sātyaki wrought a deed yet more wicked than that, in that he struck down one who, his soul resolved, had sat himself down to die by abstention.

sanskrit: eko dvābhyāṃ hataḥ śeṣe tvam adharmeṇa dhārmikaḥ iti yūpadhvajasyaitāḥ striyaḥ krośanti mādhava
english: "One, you who were righteous, were slain by two through unrighteousness, and so you lie": thus, O Mādhava, do the women of him whose banner bore the sacrificial post cry out.

sanskrit: bhāryā yūpadhvajasyaiṣā karasaṃmitamadhyamā kṛtvotsaṅge bhujaṃ bhartuḥ kṛpaṇaṃ paryadevayat
english: This wife of him whose banner bore the sacrificial post, her waist no wider than a hand may span, laying her husband's arm upon her lap, piteously lamented:

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa raśanotkarṣī pīnastanavimardanaḥ nābhyūrujaghanasparśī nīvīvisraṃsanaḥ karaḥ
english: "This is that hand which would loosen my girdle, which would press my full breasts, which would touch my navel, my thighs, my hips, and slip away the knot of my robe."

sanskrit: vāsudevasya sāṃnidhye pārthenākliṣṭakarmaṇā yudhyataḥ samare 'nyena pramattasya nipātitaḥ
english: "In the very presence of Vāsudeva, by Pārtha of untiring deeds, was he struck down while he fought another in the field, off his guard."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu vakṣyasi saṃsatsu kathāsu ca janārdana arjunasya mahat karma svayaṃ vā sa kirīṭavān
english: "What now, O Janārdana, will you tell in the assemblies and the tales of Arjuna's great deed, or what will the diademed one himself say of it?"

sanskrit: ity evaṃ garhayitvaiṣā tūṣṇīm āste varāṅganā tām etām anuśocanti sapatnyaḥ svām iva snuṣām
english: Having thus reproached him, that fair-limbed woman falls silent; and her co-wives grieve for her as for their own daughter-in-law.

sanskrit: gāndhārarājaḥ śakunir balavān satyavikramaḥ nihataḥ sahadevena bhāgineyena mātulaḥ
english: Śakuni, king of Gāndhāra, mighty and true in valor, has been slain by his sister's son Sahadeva — the uncle by the nephew.

sanskrit: yaḥ purā hemadaṇḍābhyāṃ vyajanābhyāṃ sma vījyate sa eṣa pakṣibhiḥ pakṣaiḥ śayāna upavījyate
english: He who once was fanned with two fans on golden staves now lies there and is fanned by the wings of birds.

sanskrit: yaḥ sma rūpāṇi kurute śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ tasya māyāvino māyā dagdhāḥ pāṇḍavatejasā
english: He who would take on shapes by the hundred and by the thousand — the illusions of that master of illusion have been burned away by the splendor of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: māyayā nikṛtiprajño jitavān yo yudhiṣṭhiram sabhāyāṃ vipulaṃ rājyaṃ sa punar jīvitaṃ jitaḥ
english: He whose cunning skill in deceit won from Yudhiṣṭhira his vast kingdom in the assembly hall through trickery has now in turn been won out of his very life.

sanskrit: śakuntāḥ śakuniṃ kṛṣṇa samantāt paryupāsate kitavaṃ mama putrāṇāṃ vināśāyopaśikṣitam
english: The birds, O Kṛṣṇa, gather all about Śakuni, that gambler schooled for the destruction of my sons.

sanskrit: etenaitan mahad vairaṃ prasaktaṃ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha vadhāya mama putrāṇām ātmanaḥ sagaṇasya ca
english: By him was this great enmity kindled with the Pāṇḍavas, for the slaying of my sons, and of himself, and of all his kin.

sanskrit: yathaiva mama putrāṇāṃ lokāḥ śastrajitāḥ prabho evam asyāpi durbuddher lokāḥ śastreṇa vai jitāḥ
english: As the worlds were won by the sword for my sons, O lord, so too for this evil-minded one have the worlds been won by the sword.

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca nāyaṃ tatrāpi putrān me bhrātṛbhiḥ saha virodhayed ṛjuprajñān anṛjur madhusūdana
english: And how, O slayer of Madhu, may this crooked one not even there set my straight-minded sons at strife with their brothers?

sanskrit: gāndhāry uvāca kāmbojaṃ paśya durdharṣaṃ kāmbojāstaraṇocitam śayānam ṛṣabhaskandhaṃ hataṃ pāṃsuśu mādhava
english: Gāndhārī said: Behold the unassailable Kāmboja, accustomed to coverlets of Kāmboja make, lying slain in the dust, his shoulders broad as a bull's, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: yasya kṣatajasaṃdigdhau bāhū candanarūṣitau avekṣya kṛpaṇaṃ bhāryā vilapaty atiduḥkhitā
english: Gazing upon his two arms, smeared with blood and anointed with sandal, his wife, stricken with utmost grief, laments piteously.

sanskrit: imau tau parighaprakhyau bāhū śubhatalāṅgulī yayor vivaram āpannāṃ na ratir māṃ purājahat
english: "These are those two arms, like iron bars, their palms and fingers fair, in whose embrace, when I came to it, delight never of old forsook me."

sanskrit: kāṃ gatiṃ nu gamiṣyāmi tvayā hīnā janeśvara dūrabandhur anātheva atīva madhurasvarā
english: "To what refuge shall I go now, bereft of you, O lord of men?" — so cries she of voice exceedingly sweet, her kinsfolk far away, like one without a protector.

sanskrit: ātape klāmyamānānāṃ vividhānām iva srajām klāntānām api nārīṇāṃ na śrīr jahati vai tanum
english: Like garlands of many kinds wilting in the heat, the women too are wearied; yet even so their beauty does not forsake their bodies.

sanskrit: śayānam abhitaḥ śūraṃ kāliṅgaṃ madhusūdana paśya dīptāṅgadayugapratibaddhamahābhujam
english: Behold the hero of Kaliṅga lying near at hand, O slayer of Madhu, his great arms clasped with a pair of gleaming armlets.

sanskrit: māgadhānām adhipatiṃ jayatsenaṃ janārdana parivārya praruditā māgadhyaḥ paśya yoṣitaḥ
english: Behold the women of Magadha, O Janārdana, gathered weeping round Jayatsena, the lord of the Māgadhas.

sanskrit: āsām āyatanetrāṇāṃ susvarāṇāṃ janārdana manaḥśrutiharo nādo mano mohayatīva me
english: The wail of these wide-eyed, sweet-voiced women, O Janārdana, ravishing both heart and hearing, seems to bewilder my very mind.

sanskrit: prakīrṇasarvābharaṇā rudantyaḥ śokakarśitāḥ svāstīrṇaśayanopetā māgadhyaḥ śerate bhuvi
english: Their every ornament scattered, weeping, wasted with grief, the women of Magadha, who once had well-spread couches, now lie upon the bare ground.

sanskrit: kosalānām adhipatiṃ rājaputraṃ bṛhadbalam bhartāraṃ parivāryaitāḥ pṛthak praruditāḥ striyaḥ
english: Round Bṛhadbala, the prince and lord of the Kosalas, their husband, these women stand and weep, each apart.

sanskrit: asya gātragatān bāṇān kārṣṇibāhubalārpitān uddharanty asukhāviṣṭā mūrchamānāḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Filled with anguish, they draw forth the arrows lodged in his limbs, driven there by the might of Kṛṣṇa's son's arm, swooning again and again.

sanskrit: āsāṃ sarvānavadyānām ātapena pariśramāt pramlānanalinābhāni bhānti vaktrāṇi mādhava
english: The faces of these wholly faultless women, weary with the heat and toil, shine like faded lotuses, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: droṇena nihatāḥ śūrāḥ śerate rucirāṅgadāḥ droṇenābhimukhāḥ sarve bhrātaraḥ pañca kekayāḥ
english: Slain by Droṇa, the heroes lie there with their splendid armlets, all five Kekaya brothers, fallen facing Droṇa.

sanskrit: taptakāñcanavarmāṇas tāmradhvajarathasrajaḥ bhāsayanti mahīṃ bhāsā jvalitā iva pāvakāḥ
english: Clad in mail of refined gold, with banners of copper hue and chariot-garlands, they light up the earth with their radiance, like blazing fires.

sanskrit: droṇena drupadaṃ saṃkhye paśya mādhava pātitam mahādvipam ivāraṇye siṃhena mahatā hatam
english: Behold Drupada struck down by Droṇa in the battle, O Mādhava, like a great elephant of the forest slain by a mighty lion.

sanskrit: pāñcālarājño vipulaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣa pāṇḍuram ātapatraṃ samābhāti śaradīva divākaraḥ
english: The broad white parasol of the Pāñcāla king, O lotus-eyed one, shines forth like the sun in the autumn sky.

sanskrit: etās tu drupadaṃ vṛddhaṃ snuṣā bhāryāś ca duḥkhitāḥ dagdhvā gacchanti pāñcālyaṃ rājānam apasavyataḥ
english: And these grieving daughters-in-law and wives, having burned aged Drupada, the Pāñcāla king, go round him keeping him on their left.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭaketuṃ maheṣvāsaṃ cedipuṃgavam aṅganāḥ droṇena nihataṃ śūraṃ haranti hṛtacetasaḥ
english: The women, their senses bereft, bear away the hero Dhṛṣṭaketu, the great archer, that bull of the Cedis, slain by Droṇa.

sanskrit: droṇāstram abhihatyaiṣa vimarde madhusūdana maheṣvāso hataḥ śete nadyā hṛta iva drumaḥ
english: Having struck back against Droṇa's weapon in the press of battle, O slayer of Madhu, this great archer lies slain, like a tree carried away by a river.

sanskrit: eṣa cedipatiḥ śūro dhṛṣṭaketur mahārathaḥ śete vinihataḥ saṃkhye hatvā śatrūn sahasraśaḥ
english: This brave lord of the Cedis, Dhṛṣṭaketu, the mighty chariot-warrior, lies slain in the battle, having slain his foes by the thousand.

sanskrit: vitudyamānaṃ vihagais taṃ bhāryāḥ pratyupasthitāḥ cedirājaṃ hṛṣīkeśa hataṃ sabalabāndhavam
english: Around him, his body torn by birds, his wives stand gathered, O Hṛṣīkeśa — round the king of the Cedis, slain together with his forces and his kinsmen.

sanskrit: dāśārhīputrajaṃ vīraṃ śayānaṃ satyavikramam āropyāṅke rudanty etāś cedirājavarāṅganāḥ
english: These fair women of the Cedi king's household, taking upon their laps the hero born of the Dāśārha woman's son, true in valor, as he lies there, weep aloud.

sanskrit: asya putraṃ hṛṣīkeśa suvaktraṃ cārukuṇḍalam droṇena samare paśya nikṛttaṃ bahudhā śaraiḥ
english: Behold his son, O Hṛṣīkeśa, fair of face and wearing lovely earrings, cut to pieces in the battle by Droṇa's arrows.

sanskrit: pitaraṃ nūnam ājisthaṃ yudhyamānaṃ paraiḥ saha nājahāt pṛṣṭhato vīram adyāpi madhusūdana
english: Surely, even to this day, O slayer of Madhu, the brave youth did not forsake the rear of his father, who stood in the fray fighting against his foes.
